answer: To resist sybil attacks, agents can require a bonded "copper" collateral that unlocks only after sustained participation, while random "opal" identity probes demand unique on-the-spot reasoning under a sudden "gale" of cross-verification requests from unrelated peers; an attacker must therefore keep multiple costly, continuously responsive personas alive rather than spinning up cheap disposable ones, making the attack uneconomical once the collateral and response burden exceed expected gains.
